small_guidance:
- Add larger tile configs to the autotune list now that the kernel compiles cleanly: e.g. `(BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=4/8, num_stages=2)` and `(BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=4, num_stages=3)` — OC=32 is small so BLOCK_M>32 just wastes work, but BLOCK_N can grow since OUT_SP=30·62·62≈115k is huge. Focus the sweep on BLOCK_N∈{128,256} with BLOCK_M=32.
- K_TOTAL = 8·27 = 216 is small; try `BLOCK_K=32` and `BLOCK_K=54` (or 27) so the K loop has only 4-8 iterations and the inner `tl.dot` is fully utilized; also try unrolling by setting `BLOCK_K=K_TOTAL` padded to 256 with masking.
- Swap program-id mapping so `program_id(0)` iterates the (N, OC-tile) axis (small) and `program_id(1)` iterates spatial tiles, then drop `GROUP_SP` swizzle — with OC=32 and BLOCK_M=32 there is only 1 OC tile, so the current swizzle is a no-op and the launch grid layout could be flattened for better L2 reuse of the weight tile across N.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a channels-last (NDHWC) layout for both input and output so the GEMM-K dimension (IC·KD·KH·KW) has IC as the innermost contiguous axis. The current NCDHW gather strides IC by ID·IH·IW which kills coalescing on the x-load; NDHWC lets a single 128-bit load fetch IC contiguous channels per spatial point.
- Make the kernel persistent over the batch dimension: with N=64 and only 1 OC tile, launch one program per (spatial-tile) and have it loop over N reusing the loaded weight tile in registers/SMEM. This amortizes the 32×216 weight load (which is tiny — fits entirely in registers) across all 64 batch elements.
- Consider a direct-conv formulation rather than im2col-GEMM: with KD=KH=KW=3 and IC=8, the K dimension is only 216 and the kernel is bandwidth-bound on the input gather. A program that tiles (OC, OH, OW) with OD/N in an outer loop and explicitly unrolls the 3×3×3×8 kernel can reuse halo input rows across adjacent OW outputs (input-stationary), cutting redundant global loads ~9×.
